{{Short description|Dutch theoretical physicist (1936–2023)}}
'''Hans Willem Capel''' (3 June 1936 – 7 April 2023) was a Dutch theoretical physicist. He was a professor of theoretical physics at the [[Leiden University]] from 1979 to 1983 and subsequently the [[University of Amsterdam]] between 1983 and 1998.

==Biography==
Capel was born on 3 June 1936 in Sceaux, France.<ref name=leiden>{{cite web|author= |url=http://hoogleraren.leidenuniv.nl/id/411 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171227122153/http://hoogleraren.leidenuniv.nl/id/411 |title=Hans Willem Capel |publisher=Leiden University |date= |archive-date=27 December 2017}}</ref> He obtained his PhD in mathematics and physics at [[Leiden University]] in 1965 under {{Interlanguage link multi|Sybren Ruurds de Groot|de}} with a dissertation titled: ''The hole-equivalence principle, the Van Vleck relation and the application to the theory of d-ions in Ligand fields''.<ref name=uva>{{cite web|url=http://albumacademicum.uva.nl/id/id002914 |title=Prof. dr. H.W. Capel, 1936 - |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200213223210/https://albumacademicum.uva.nl/id/id002914 |publisher=University of Amsterdam|archive-date=13 February 2020}}</ref><ref name="AIP Publishing 2023 p. 0922a">{{cite journal | title=Hans Capel | url=https://pubs.aip.org/physicstoday/online/42715/Hans-Capel |journal=Physics Today | publisher=AIP Publishing | volume=2023 | issue=09 | date=2023-09-27 | issn=1945-0699 | doi=10.1063/pt.6.4o.20230922a | article-number=0922a| url-access=subscription }}</ref> Capel subsequently became a lector of theoretical physics at the same university in 1970, and served as professor in the same field between 1979 and 1983.<ref name=leiden/> He then switchted to the University of Amsterdam where he continued in the same field and was professor from 1983 to 1998.<ref name=uva/> He worked another three years at the university without reimbursement.<ref name=uva/>

Capel is well known for introducing, in [[statistical physics]], the ''Blume-Capel model'', describing [[tricritical point]]s. Apart from to statistical mechanics, he made important contributions to many fields of physics, especially in the theory of integrable systems (in particular discrete integrable systems) and dynamical systems theory. During his career he was doctoral advisor to 21 PhD students.<ref name="AIP Publishing 2023 p. 0922a"/>

Capel was elected a member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1990.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://knaw.nl/en/members/members/3976 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171226122234/https://knaw.nl/en/members/members/3976 |title=Hans Capel |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |archive-date=26 December 2017}}</ref> He also served as editor of [[Physica (journal)|Physica A]].<ref name="AIP Publishing 2023 p. 0922a"/>

Capel died in [[Haarlem]] on 7 April 2023 after a short illness.<ref name="AIP Publishing 2023 p. 0922a"/>
